# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Puzzles

---

## I. Region/Area Division Puzzles
*Puzzles where the primary mechanic involves partitioning the grid into defined regions or shapes*

### A. Polyomino-Based Division
*Regions must conform to specific polyomino shapes or size rules*

- **Fillomino** — divide grid into polyominoes where each region's size matches its numbered cells
- **Five Cells** — divide grid into pentominoes
- **LITS** — shade one tetromino per region such that shaded cells form a connected group
- **Norinori** — shade two cells per region such that every shaded cell is part of a domino
- **Evolomino** — regions evolve in size by exactly one cell from neighbors
- **Chained Block** — divide into rectangular blocks chained in sequence

### B. Rectangular Division
*Regions must be rectangles or follow strict geometric constraints*

- **Shikaku** — divide grid into rectangles, each containing exactly one number indicating its area
- **Double Choco** — divide into regions each containing equal white and shaded halves of identical shape

### C. General Region Coloring / Shading Division
*Regions defined by shading rules without strict shape requirements*

- **Nurikabe** — shade cells to form "rivers" isolating numbered island regions
- **Heyawake** — shade cells with constraints on runs and region counts
- **Hitori** — eliminate duplicate numbers by shading cells, no shaded cells adjacent
- **Tilepaint** — shade cells so each rectangular region is entirely shaded or unshaded
- **Nuritwin** — shade cells forming two congruent connected shapes
- **Nurimeizu** — shade cells to create a maze-like path structure
- **Nurimisaki** — shade cells leaving unshaded "cape" cells satisfying directional clues
- **Choco Banana** — shade cells so all shaded regions are rectangles and all unshaded regions are non-rectangular (or vice versa)
- **Sto-stone** — place stones in regions so shaded stones fall and stack correctly

---

## II. Number Placement Puzzles
*Puzzles where the primary mechanic involves placing or deducing numbers in cells*

### A. Latin Square / Uniqueness Constraints
*Each number appears exactly once per row, column, or region*

- **Sudoku** — place 1–9 in every row, column, and 3×3 box without repetition
- **Ripple Effect** — fill regions with 1–N; identical numbers in same row/column must be separated by distance ≥ their value
- **Makaro** — fill regions with 1–N; arrows in cells indicate the direction of the largest number in that region

### B. Numbered Cell / Clue Satisfaction
*Numbers in the grid act as clues that constrain surrounding or connected cells*

- **Kurodoko** — place black cells so numbered white cells see exactly that many white cells in their row/column
- **Usowan** — some clues are liars; determine which clues are false while satisfying shading rules
- **Kurotto** — shade cells so each circled number equals the total count of shaded cells in connected shaded groups touching it
- **Nansuke** — assign numbers to regions based on shape-matching and size logic

---

## III. Path and Loop Puzzles
*Puzzles where the primary mechanic involves drawing paths, loops, or connected routes through the grid*

### A. Single Closed Loop
*A single continuous loop must be drawn through the grid*

- **Slitherlink** — draw a single closed loop along grid edges; numbers indicate how many sides of each cell are used
- **Masyu** — draw a loop passing through all circles; black circles turn, white circles go straight
- **Moon-or-Sun** — draw a loop alternating between moon and sun regions, changing type at each region boundary
- **Mid-loop** — draw a loop that passes through the midpoint of specific edges
- **Dotchi-Loop** — draw a loop that passes through cells, satisfying either/or directional constraints

### B. Multiple Paths / Open Paths
*Multiple separate paths or open-ended routes are drawn*

- **Numberlink** — connect matching numbered pairs with non-crossing, non-overlapping paths that fill the grid
- **Pencils** — draw straight-line paths ("pencils") from clue cells that fill the grid without overlap
- **Nagareru** — draw paths that flow in a consistent direction through clue constraints
- **Suraromu** — draw paths through cells satisfying directional and length constraints

### C. Path with Special Movement Rules
*Paths follow specific movement or transformation rules*

- **Hebi** — draw a snake-shaped path of a given length satisfying numbered clues
- **Satogaeri** — return circles to their home regions by moving along paths without crossing
- **Yosenabe** — move numbered pieces along paths so they gather into groups summing to target values

---

## IV. Bridge and Connection Puzzles
*Puzzles where the primary mechanic involves connecting nodes or islands*

- **Hashiwokakero** — connect numbered islands with bridges; bridge count must match island numbers, all islands connected
- **Akari** — place lightbulbs in white cells to illuminate the entire grid without bulbs seeing each other

---

## V. Directional and Orientation Puzzles
*Puzzles where the primary mechanic involves assigning directions, orientations, or angles to cells*

- **Juosan** — draw horizontal or vertical lines in each cell; lines in the same row/column must all be the same orientation
- **Sashigane** — draw L-shaped paths (sashigane) in the grid satisfying numbered and directional clues
- **Shakashaka** — place diagonal half-shaded triangles in white cells so all unshaded areas form rectangles
- **Yajilin** — shade cells and draw a single loop; arrow clues indicate the count of shaded cells in a given direction

---

## VI. Hybrid / Multi-Mechanic Puzzles
*Puzzles that combine two or more primary mechanics in roughly equal measure*

- **Heyawake** *(also listed under I.C)* — shading interacts with region-count and path-blocking rules
- **Kurodoko** *(also listed under II.B)* — number satisfaction combined with connectivity of white cells
- **Dotchi-Loop** *(also listed under III.A)* — loop drawing combined with binary choice clues per cell

> *Note: Several puzzles appear in a single primary category above; cross-references here highlight puzzles whose mechanics span multiple categories.*

---

## Summary Table

| Category | Puzzles |
|---|---|
| **I.A Polyomino Division** | Fillomino, Five Cells, LITS, Norinori, Evolomino, Chained Block |
| **I.B Rectangular Division** | Shikaku, Double Choco |
| **I.C Shading/Region Coloring** | Nurikabe, Heyawake, Hitori, Tilepaint, Nuritwin, Nurimeizu, Nurimisaki, Choco Banana, Sto-stone |
| **II.A Latin Square** | Sudoku, Ripple Effect, Makaro |
| **II.B Numbered Clue Satisfaction** | Kurodoko, Usowan, Kurotto, Nansuke |
| **III.A Single Closed Loop** | Slitherlink, Masyu, Moon-or-Sun, Mid-loop, Dotchi-Loop |
| **III.B Multiple/Open Paths** | Numberlink, Pencils, Nagareru, Suraromu |
| **III.C Special Movement Paths** | Hebi, Satogaeri, Yosenabe |
| **IV. Bridge & Connection** | Hashiwokakero, Akari |
| **V. Directional & Orientation** | Juosan, Sashigane, Shakashaka, Yajilin |
